title: Cross-region quantized model failover: preflight & execution runbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: Procedure and automated checks to safely perform a cross-region failover when running quantized model variants. Emphasizes preflight verification of quantized kernels, KV cache compatibility, SLO guardrails, capacity estimates, and telemetry-driven execution to avoid cascading degradation.
body:
Purpose
This runbook describes the preflight checks, decision criteria, execution steps, verification, and rollback conditions for performing a cross-region failover when the target replicas are running quantized model variants. It is intended for SREs executing or approving a cross-region migration of live inference traffic and for engineers designing automated failover pipelines.

Scope and assumptions
- Scope: live inference endpoints (text generation, chat, embeddings) using Redwood serving runtime.
- Assumptions: target region has compatible GPU instance classes, the quantized model artifact has been validated by the model-onboarding team, and CI artifact tags are available (example: model:v3-q8_hem8).
- Not in scope: full model retraining, schema migrations to client payloads, or customer-facing communications templates (see Customer Success playbook).

Key contacts and ownership
- Runbook owner: eng-sre (oncall rotation)
- Preflight validation owner: eng-serving-runtime / model-onboarding
- Network & routing owner: eng-infra
- Escalation: paging to SRE lead and runtime lead if failover takes longer than 15 minutes or SLO alert fires during execution

SLO and error-budget guardrails
- Primary SLOs for decision gating:
  1) P95 latency <= 450ms (generation endpoints)
  2) Request success rate >= 99.6% over 5m window
  3) Token compute tail (95->99 delta) < 30% of baseline
- Error budget policy (for failover window): if error budget consumption > 15% in 24h window AND 5m success rate < 99.0%, abort failover and follow degradation containment procedure.

Preflight checklist (automated checks recommended first; manual gates second)
| Check | Required state | Owner | Verification command / query |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Model binary signature matches CI tag | match | model-onboarding | sha256sum model-v3-q8_hem8.pt | cut -d ' ' -f1 |
| Kernel compatibility table entries exist for target GPU | yes | eng-serving-runtime | curl -s $KERNEL_REGISTRY/compat/model-v3-q8_hem8 | jq .supported_gpus |
| KV cache format compatibility | match schema v2 | eng-serving-runtime | python tools/kv_check.py --artifact model-v3-q8_hem8 | jq .result |
| End-to-end synthetic canary (cold start) | p95 < 600ms, success 100% | SRE canary job | ./ci/canary/run_canary.sh --region=eu-west-1 --model=model:v3-q8_hem8 |
| Memory/resident set for quantized artifact | < 85% GPU memory used at warm-pool size | eng-sre | nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv -l 1 |
| Inference throughput headroom estimate | >= planned QPS * 1.25 | eng-sre/capacity | python tools/throughput_estimator.py --model model-v3-q8_hem8 --seq 128 --qps $expected_qps |
| Observability hooks (traces, token-level metrics) active | yes | eng-platform | curl $OBS_ENDPOINT/health |

Preflight automation and canary plan
1. Run CI artifact validation pipeline (automated): signature, kernel compat, KV format, minimal integration smoke tests. Failure stops here.
2. Start synthetic canary suite against a staging pool in the target region:
   - Canary scenario A: short prompts (seq 64), 500 requests at 20 RPS.
   - Canary scenario B: long prompts (seq 512), 200 requests at 5 RPS (cold starts).
   - Collect: latency percentiles, OOMs, GPU util, model logits checksum.
3. If canaries meet thresholds, automatically create an incremental traffic plan (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 20m windows). If any step triggers an SLO alert, pause and run the mitigation checklist.

Capacity estimation & headroom calculation (example)
- Inputs: expected steady QPS (Q), average tokens per request (T), p95 token latency per token (L_tok), replicas R.
- Required token throughput = Q * T.
- Tokens per GPU per second = 1 / L_tok * concurrency_factor.
- Minimal replicas = ceil( (Q * T) / (tokens_per_gpu) * safety_factor ) where safety_factor = 1.25 for bursty traffic.
Example command to compute replicas:
python tools/replica_calc.py --qps 120 --avg_tokens 80 --latency_per_token_ms 0.9 --safety 1.25

Decision matrix (summary)
- If any preflight check fails: abort, reopen artifact validation with model-onboarding.
- If canary cold-starts show p95 > 2x baseline: abort and consult runtime team (possible kernel regression).
- If memory utilization > 90% at warm pool size: shrink warm pool or increase instance class; do not failover.
- If canary passes but first incremental traffic step breaches SLO: move back to previous traffic percentage and throttle traffic for 30m while investigating.

Execution steps (operator-driven or automated pipeline)
1. Announce planned window on #sre-ops with timestamp and rollback window.
2. Ensure all preflight checks are green.
3. Update routing policy: add target region route with weight 5% (or use traffic-shaper api).
   - CLI example: redwoodctl route update --endpoint /v1/generate --add-region eu-west-1 --weight 5
4. Monitor telemetry for 5 minutes: latency, success rate, GPU OOMs, tail-token-latency. Use dashboards named "Cross-region failover — <endpoint>".
5. If stable, increase to 25% after 10 minutes, then 50% after another 10, then 100%.
6. After 100% shift, keep both regions live for 30m for progressive validation, then decommission old region if stable.

Mitigation checklist (if an aggressive metric fires)
- Immediate: reduce weight by 50%, or remove target region route and revert to source region.
- If errors spike but latency stable: enable degraded-mode cache (prefix cache read-only) to reduce recompute.
- If memory OOMs observed: scale up instance class or reduce warm pool by 30%.
- If model quality regression (logit checksum drift > 1%): rollback routing immediately and open a model-onboarding incident.

Verification & post-failover validation
- Run the full synthetic canary again against the live target pool with traffic shaping to simulate production distribution.
- Validate customer-facing metrics: per-tenant success-rate, latency, and quality evals (a small set of golden prompts run through both regions and compared with tolerance thresholds).
- Confirm billing/quotas are within expected range for committed capacity.

Rollback criteria and procedure
- Rollback triggers (any of these): sustained success rate < 99% for 10m, p95 > 2x baseline for 10m, OOMs observed on >1% of requests in 5m, or evidence of model output corruption.
- Rollback steps:
  1. Immediately set route weight back to previous region (CLI: redwoodctl route update --remove-region eu-west-1).
  2. Notify stakeholders (#sre-ops, runtime, product).
  3. Keep target region pool alive for forensic captures for at least 2h.
  4. Trigger incident review and capture artifacts (see Incident evidence collection below).

Incident evidence collection (required fields)
- Time window and exact routing change events (UTC).
- Canary job logs and synthetic payloads.
- Prometheus timeseries for: request_success_rate, p95_latency, token_tail_latency, gpu_memory_util, kv_cache_miss_rate.
- Sampled request/response pairs (sanitized).
- Model artifact hashes and kernel registry response at time of deployment.

Runbook automation recommendations
- Implement a preflight pipeline that gates automatic traffic increases on canary metrics (CI/CD style).
- Add a Machine-Readable Decision Point (MRDP) that aborts automation if any of the SLO guardrails are violated.
- Expose a single CLI that runs all preflight checks and prints a pass/fail summary: redwoodctl failover preflight --region eu-west-1 --model model:v3-q8_hem8

Postmortem and continuous improvement
- For every executed failover (successful or rolled back), owner must create a 1-page incident summary with: timeline, root cause (if any), lessons learned, and at least one concrete follow-up (owners and due dates).
- Maintain a short-running experiment plan for quantized kernels (weekly regression canaries against a small traffic slice) to catch degradations before failovers are required.

Appendix A — Example Prometheus queries
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- success rate: 1 - sum(rate(inference_request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m]))
- GPU OOMs: sum(rate(nvidia_gpu_oom_events_total[5m])) by (instance)

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets
- Preflight run: redwoodctl failover preflight --model model:v3-q8_hem8 --region eu-west-1 --canary-config canary/short-long.yaml
- Incremental weight update: redwoodctl route set-weight --endpoint /v1/generate --region eu-west-1 --weight 25
- Force rollback: redwoodctl route remove-region --endpoint /v1/generate --region eu-west-1 --reason "rollback: p95 breach"

Appendix C — Known limitations and open issues
- Some older kernel variants do not expose token-level latency; the runbook requires an approximation until kernel telemetry is standardized.
- Cross-region routing adds ~20–40ms network latency which must be accounted for when comparing to baseline SLOs; we recommend adjusting latency baselines for cross-region tests.
- Not all customer-aware routing policies support sub-tenant weighting; consult product team for tenant-specific failovers.
